claims.explanation: Buphenine is a beta-adrenergic agonist whose growth-inhibitory activity in this screen tracks with intact adrenergic/GPCR-cAMP signaling rather than with any single lineage. The most consistent genomic pattern among sensitive lines is co-occurrence of MAPK-pathway activation (BRAF, NRAS, MAP2K1, NF1, EGFR) with PI3K/AKT-pathway alterations (PTEN loss, PIK3CA mutation), suggesting that cells with constitutive proliferative signaling and intact ADRB2-coupled cAMP signaling are selectively killed, while lines with KEAP1/NFE2L2 antioxidant-pathway activation or mesenchymal/squamous dedifferentiation are protected.

features.basis: buphenine is an ADRB2 agonist; target expression is required for response
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal/endometrial lines are enriched among sensitive lines
NRAS-mutant melanoma line IPC298 is among the most killed
MAP2K1-mutant NSCLC line NCIH1437 is among the most killed
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and appears in several sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines HCC4006, NCIH1650, NCIH1648 are sensitive
PTEN loss co-occurs with sensitive BRAF/NRAS-mutant lines
PIK3CA-mutant gastric/colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
KEAP1-mutant HEC265 is sensitive but NFE2L2 activation generally blunts oxidative stress responses
NFE2L2 activation in HEC265 and SNUC5 may limit drug-induced oxidative stress
SMARCA4-mutant lines KYSE270 and OV7 show divergent response; loss may reduce dependency
KMT2D mutations are frequent in least-affected squamous lines
